about.intro: Auro Dent is a modern dental clinic in Tirana where prevention, careful diagnosis and clear communication guide every treatment conversation.

values.title: Conservative planning
values.text: Treatment is described carefully, with oral health as the foundation.

values.title: Friendly visits
values.text: The tone is warm, organised and reassuring.

about.technology: Digital scans, clinical photography and careful treatment planning help us explain findings clearly and prepare each stage of care.
about.team: Our team brings together general dentistry, implant care, orthodontics and paediatric dentistry.

servicesPage.title: Dental services in Tirana
servicesPage.intro: Choose a treatment to learn about the process, candidacy, common questions and related services.

generalDentistry.name: General dentistry & check-ups
generalDentistry.short: Routine exams, hygiene guidance, fillings and prevention for long-term oral health.
generalDentistry.intro: General dentistry is the foundation of a healthy smile. At Auro Dent, check-ups focus on prevention, early diagnosis and clear treatment priorities.
generalDentistry.for: This service is for adults and teens who need routine exams, hygiene advice, tooth-coloured fillings or a first consultation.
process: Review dental history and current concerns.
Complete clinical exam and X-rays when needed.
Explain findings with priorities and options.
Plan prevention, hygiene or restorative care.

faqs.q: How often should I book a check-up?
faqs.a: Many patients attend every six months, but the right interval depends on gum health, decay risk and previous treatment.

faqs.q: Do I need X-rays every visit?
faqs.a: No. X-rays are recommended only when they help diagnosis or monitoring.

faqs.q: Can I book only for advice?
faqs.a: Yes. A consultation is useful before choosing treatment.

teethWhitening.name: Teeth whitening
teethWhitening.short: Professional whitening options planned after checking enamel, gums and sensitivity risk.
teethWhitening.intro: Teeth whitening can brighten natural enamel when it is planned safely. Existing crowns, fillings and veneers do not whiten like natural teeth.
teethWhitening.for: Whitening may suit adults with healthy teeth and gums who want a brighter shade before an event or cosmetic treatment.
process: Check gums, enamel and existing restorations.
Discuss shade expectations and sensitivity risk.

faqs.a: Professional whitening is planned after a dental check and should be used as directed.
No. Ceramic and composite restorations do not change shade with whitening.
Temporary sensitivity can happen, so the dentist should assess risk first.

dentalImplants.name: Dental implants
dentalImplants.short: Implant treatment planning for missing teeth, including consultation, diagnostics and restoration.
dentalImplants.intro: Dental implants can replace missing teeth when oral health, bone support and general health are suitable.
dentalImplants.for: This treatment may be considered for patients missing one or more teeth who want a fixed replacement option.
process: Healing period and final crown or bridge.

faqs.a: No. Suitability depends on bone, gums, health history and clinical examination.
Timing varies because healing and restoration stages differ by case.
Yes. Daily cleaning and professional follow-up are important.

orthodontics.name: Orthodontics, braces & aligners
orthodontics.short: Braces and clear aligner planning for tooth alignment, bite comfort and smile balance.
orthodontics.intro: Orthodontic treatment can improve tooth position and bite function using braces or clear aligners when clinically suitable.
orthodontics.for: It may suit teens or adults with crowding, spacing, relapse or bite concerns.

faqs.q: Are aligners right for every case?
faqs.a: No. Some movements require braces or specialist orthodontic care.
Treatment length depends on complexity and patient cooperation.
Yes. Retainers help maintain tooth position after treatment.

pediatricDentistry.name: Pediatric dentistry
pediatricDentistry.short: Friendly dental visits for children, prevention, sealants and parent guidance.
pediatricDentistry.intro: Children’s dentistry focuses on prevention, confidence and early habits that support lifelong oral health.
pediatricDentistry.for: This service is for children and parents who want check-ups, prevention advice or help with early dental concerns.

faqs.a: Early visits help children become comfortable and allow parents to receive prevention advice.
Yes. They support chewing, speech and spacing for adult teeth.
Daily brushing, fluoride toothpaste and limiting frequent sugar exposure help reduce risk.

emergencyCare.name: Emergency dental care
emergencyCare.short: Urgent dental assessment for pain, swelling, broken teeth and lost restorations.
emergencyCare.intro: Dental emergencies need calm triage and clear next steps. Severe pain, swelling or trauma should be assessed quickly.
emergencyCare.for: This service is for patients with toothache, swelling, broken teeth, dental trauma or lost fillings and crowns.
process: The dentist examines the area and may request imaging.
Immediate relief or temporary care is provided when appropriate.

faqs.a: Severe pain, swelling, trauma, uncontrolled bleeding or a broken front tooth should be assessed quickly.

faqs.q: Can every problem be fixed the same day?
faqs.a: Not always. The first visit may focus on diagnosis and stabilising the problem.

faqs.q: Should I wait if swelling improves?
faqs.a: Swelling can signal infection, so professional advice is recommended.

cosmeticVeneers.name: Cosmetic dentistry (veneers)
cosmeticVeneers.short: Smile design, veneers and aesthetic planning with cautious, natural-looking goals.
cosmeticVeneers.intro: Cosmetic dentistry can improve tooth shape, shade and smile harmony. Veneers are planned only after checking oral health and bite.
cosmeticVeneers.for: Veneers may suit patients with healthy teeth who want to improve visible shape, shade or spacing concerns.
process: Exam of enamel, gums and bite.

faqs.a: Many veneer treatments involve enamel preparation, so they should be considered long-term dental work.
Often yes, especially if only some teeth receive veneers.

faqs.q: Can veneers fix every smile concern?
faqs.a: No. Orthodontics, whitening or crowns may be more appropriate depending on the case.

blog.title: Dental education articles
blog.intro: Practical articles to help you make informed decisions about daily oral health and treatment options.

visitDentist.title: How often should you visit the dentist?
visitDentist.description: A practical guide to dental check-up intervals and prevention.
body: Most patients benefit from regular dental check-ups, but the ideal schedule depends on gum health, decay risk and previous treatment.
A check-up is not only about finding cavities. It also helps review brushing habits, gum inflammation, tooth wear and early symptoms.
If you have pain, bleeding gums or sensitivity, book earlier instead of waiting for the next routine visit.

whiteningExpect.title: Teeth whitening: what to expect
whiteningExpect.description: What patients should know before professional whitening.
body: Professional whitening starts with checking teeth and gums. This helps identify sensitivity risks and restorations that will not change colour.
Results vary between patients. Natural enamel, habits and previous dental work all affect the final shade.
After whitening, good hygiene and regular cleanings help maintain the result.

childrensTeeth.title: Caring for children’s teeth
childrensTeeth.description: Simple habits that support children’s oral health.
body: Children’s dental care begins with daily brushing, fluoride toothpaste and early positive visits.
Parents can reduce cavity risk by limiting frequent sugary snacks and helping children brush until they have the coordination to do it well.
A friendly first visit helps children see dental care as normal and safe.

implantAftercare.title: How to care for dental implants
implantAftercare.description: Daily and professional care after implant treatment.
body: Dental implants need daily cleaning around the gumline and regular professional checks.
Bleeding, swelling or discomfort around an implant should be assessed promptly.
Maintenance visits help monitor bite forces, gum health and the condition of the restoration.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.intro: Common patient questions before booking a dental appointment.

items.q: How do I book an appointment?
items.a: Use the booking form, call the clinic or send an email with your preferred time and treatment interest.
Emergency appointments are coordinated based on availability and symptom urgency.

items.q: Can international patients contact the clinic before travelling?
items.a: Yes. Remote enquiries can help prepare the first consultation, although final diagnosis requires an in-person exam.
Online prices are indicative. The final cost depends on your diagnosis, treatment options and individual care plan.
